page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server within the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 96 virtual CPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes 23,038 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and it is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read operations reaching 7,287.47 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 229.38 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations scale effectively, as demonstrated by top-tier results in bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Redis SET operations, which achieved 122.77 million operations per second. Single-core performance sits in the top 25%, showing a slight relative tradeoff compared to its multi-core capabilities.

Given the high local NVMe SSD storage capacity and strong multi-core performance, this server is designed for large-scale database operations, data warehousing, and heavy transactional workloads. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high memory bandwidth also make it suitable for memory-intensive applications and large-scale software compilation. From a resource density perspective, the integration of massive local NVMe storage alongside a high-core-count AMD EPYC processor provides a consolidated hardware profile that reduces the need for external storage attachments, optimizing cost efficiency for storage-heavy and database workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity server from the Lasv4 family, featuring 96 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this server delivers top-tier multi-core performance, as evidenced by its top 10% rankings in PassMark CPU, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, particularly for cached small-block reads. While single-core performance is strong, the hardware profile is heavily optimized for parallel processing and data-intensive tasks. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring dense local storage and high memory capacity, making it an excellent fit for large-scale databases, Redis deployments, and heavy multi-threaded data processing.
